2.0.0.en: Major update: rebuilt the app with python and use a new authentication library to hopefully resolve connection issues. Requires Homey firmware v13 or newer. One-time action: open the app settings and sign in again with your email, password and authenticator (2-step) code — your region is now detected automatically. New: 'Say with Voice' flow action with Amazon Polly voices, plus improved whisper. If you used the 'Run Routine' flow card, please re-select your routine.

2.0.1.en: Major update: the app has been rebuilt in Python with a new authentication library to fix the recurring connection drops. Requires Homey firmware v13 or newer. One-time action: open the app settings and sign in again with your email, password and authenticator (2-step) code — your region is now detected automatically. New: 'Say with Voice' flow action with Amazon Polly voices, plus improved whisper. If you used the 'Run Routine' flow card, please re-select your routine. Also fixes adding devices, playback controls and now-playing updates.

2.0.2.en: Major update: the app has been rebuilt in Python with a new authentication library to fix the recurring connection drops. Requires Homey firmware v13 or newer. One-time action: open the app settings and sign in again with your email, password and authenticator (2-step) code — your region is now detected automatically. New: 'Say with Voice' flow action with Amazon Polly voices, plus improved whisper. If you used the 'Run Routine' flow card, please re-select your routine. Also fixes adding devices, playback controls and now-playing updates.

2.0.3.en: More reliable sign-in: if Amazon returns an unexpected page instead of the code prompt, the app now retries automatically. Added an optional 'diagnostic logging' switch in app settings — if you have trouble signing in or connecting, turn it on, reproduce the problem, then send a diagnostic report so the cause can be pinpointed. Also updated the Amazon library to the latest version, which fixes playback (play/pause/next/previous) controls.

2.0.4.en: Major reliability update for signing in and adding devices. Fixed sign-in failing with 'Cannot find account owner customer ID' (which affected accounts that had signed in several times), and fixed 'Add device' timing out while searching — adding devices, and loading them at sign-in, is now much faster. Sign-in is also saved as soon as your account is registered so a brief Amazon hiccup no longer makes you start over, the app retries automatically if Amazon returns an unexpected page, and error messages are clearer. New: an optional 'diagnostic logging' switch in app settings to help pin down connection problems. Also updated the underlying Amazon library, which fixes playback (play/pause/next/previous) controls.

2.1.0.en: New: Do Not Disturb. Every Echo now has a Do Not Disturb toggle, plus flow cards to switch it on or off, check whether it's on, and start a flow when it changes — so you can silence notifications, announcements and calls at night and turn them back on in the morning. Alarms, timers and reminders still ring, and switching Do Not Disturb from the Alexa app or by voice updates Homey straight away. New: screen controls for devices that have a screen (Echo Show, Echo Spot, Echo Dot with clock). Turn the display on or off, set its brightness, and switch adaptive brightness on or off, each with matching flow cards. These controls appear automatically, and only on devices that actually support them. Changes you make in the Alexa app or by voice are picked up too. Also updated the underlying Amazon library and made reconnecting faster by skipping a redundant account lookup that was running on every refresh.

2.1.1.en: Fixes an empty routine list in the 'Run Routine' flow card. On some accounts the app stayed connected to the wrong Amazon country after signing in, which made Amazon return no routines at all and made spoken messages come out in US English — while everything else kept working, so nothing looked wrong. The app now re-checks which Amazon country your account belongs to every time it reconnects and corrects itself, so the routine list and the spoken language come good on their own; no need to sign in again. Also: routines that Amazon returns without a name no longer hide your whole routine list, the card reports a clear error instead of quietly doing nothing when the routine it was set to can no longer be found, and diagnostic reports now show which Amazon region and account your Homey is talking to. If your routine list is still empty, please send a diagnostic report from the app settings (no need to switch on diagnostic logging first).

2.1.2.en: Fixes spoken messages failing silently right after signing in: 'Say', 'Announce', 'Say with Voice', sounds and routines did nothing at all (Amazon rejected them) until the app happened to restart. New: an 'Amazon server' setting. Leave it on Auto — the app asks Amazon which server your account belongs to — and pick a country only if connecting fails because your network cannot reach that server; some routers and ad/tracker filters cannot look up the address of alexa.amazon.fr and similar regional servers. Choosing a country changes only which server the app talks to: spoken messages keep the language of your own Amazon account, so nothing starts speaking a different language. Clearer errors too: when a server address cannot be looked up, the app now names it and points at your router's DNS instead of just saying it cannot reach Amazon, and a sign-in that Amazon turns down now asks you to check the 2-step verification code instead of showing a technical error message. Also fixes live updates (volume, playback and Do Not Disturb changes made elsewhere) staying dead after a failed connection attempt, which previously needed an app restart.

2.1.3.en: Fixes spoken messages failing silently right after signing in: 'Say', 'Announce', 'Say with Voice', sounds and routines did nothing at all (Amazon rejected them) until the app happened to restart. New: an 'Amazon server' setting. Leave it on Auto — the app asks Amazon which server your account belongs to — and pick a country only if connecting fails because your network cannot reach that server; some routers and ad/tracker filters cannot look up the address of alexa.amazon.fr and similar regional servers. Choosing a country changes only which server the app talks to: spoken messages keep the language of your own Amazon account, so nothing starts speaking a different language. Clearer errors too: when a server address cannot be looked up, the app now names it and points at your router's DNS instead of just saying it cannot reach Amazon, and a sign-in that Amazon turns down now asks you to check the 2-step verification code instead of showing a technical error message. Also fixes live updates (volume, playback and Do Not Disturb changes made elsewhere) staying dead after a failed connection attempt, which previously needed an app restart. The Amazon server setting now also applies while signing in, so it can be used to work around a network that cannot reach your own regional Amazon server.

2.1.4.en: The app now asks your network for Amazon's address far less often. Some home routers stop answering after a burst of lookups, which made the app fail to connect or a Flow card fail to run even though the internet was fine. Trying again after a failed sign-in no longer starts from scratch either. When a lookup does fail, app settings and Flow cards now say which address could not be resolved instead of showing a technical error.

2.1.5.en: If Amazon stops accepting the connection after the app has been running for a while, the app now renews the connection and carries out the command anyway, instead of leaving Flow cards failing until you restart the app.

2.1.6.en: Adds a 'Run network test' button to app settings. If the app cannot reach Amazon, this records exactly how your Homey looks up Amazon's addresses and what your network answers, so the result shows up in a diagnostic report. The app also runs this check by itself when a lookup fails and diagnostic logging is switched on. Volume and playback changes made elsewhere also show up faster, because the app no longer waits on voice history data it never used.
